To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the minute vasculatures of psychiatric patients are abnormally reactive to stimuli, and that this reactivity is associated with a progressive anoxia of the adjacent intervascular tissue cells.
in mental disease there is a progressive increase in capillary pressure, a progressive decrease in the local blood-oxygen tension and a progressive increase in tissue-cell anoxia.

in the peripheral tissues of psychiatric patients, and particularly of psychotics, a progressive and reversible anoxic state of the intervascular cells occurs in association with a progressive and reversible increase of the capillary pressure, decrease of the local blood-oxygenation and decrease of the capillary corpuscular blood-flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the vascular and cellular responses in the skin of patients and the dynamic changes in their mental states.
the relationship between the blood-histamine and tissue-cell anoxia of the capillary vascular system in mental illness and the mental state of such patients.
the relationship between the vascular and cellular changes and the mental state of patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these changes occur in the peripheral capillaries and the adjacent tissue cells of patients with schizophrenia, and of patients with other mental disorders, when they are in a state of acute psychosis or other mental disturbance.
, in mental disease, there is an abnormal response of the capillary vascular system which, in turn, is reflected by a series of changes in the tissue-cellular elements of the brain.
these vascular and cellular reactions seem to be a manifestation of a state of tissue-cell anoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pathophysiological reactions of the capillary vascular system in mental illness are associated in a dynamic fashion with the state of consciousness of the patient.
the vascular and cellular responses of these patients to their own blood and tissue fluids are not normal, and that these responses are related to their mental state.

the capillaries of patients suffering from schizophrenia and related disorders have an increased propensity to become abnormally dilated, and that this propensity is associated with a tendency for the adjacent intervascular tissue cells to become swollen and degenerated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capillary vasculature of the brain and other organs of the body, in the case of the mentally ill, is in a state of continuous and progressive dysfunction and degeneration.
the vascular changes we have been studying are not the cause of mental disease, but are a manifestation of a disturbed state of the mind.
the tissue-cell anoxia, which is the result of the aberrant vascular responses, may play an important part in the pathogenesis of the mental disease.
